prerequisiteBridge: A Hopfield network reduces each neuron to \(S_{i}\in {-1,+1}\). A memory pattern \(\xi ^{\mu }\) is likewise a vector of N signs. Encoding writes patterns into symmetric weights using outer products. Retrieval begins from a partial or noisy cue; one neuron at a time is set to the sign of its weighted input until no unit changes. This is an abstract associative memory, not a model of exact biological spike timing.

Energy is a scalar landscape over network states. With symmetric weights and asynchronous updates, every actual flip leaves E unchanged or lowers it, so a trajectory eventually reaches a local minimum. A local minimum is a fixed point but need not be the intended memory: antipatterns, odd mixtures, and spin-glass states can also be minima. Pattern completion occurs when the initial state lies inside the target memory's basin.

When several random patterns are stored, the local field during retrieval contains target signal plus crosstalk from the other patterns. After normalization by N, target signal is about 1 and the total variance of many independent interference terms is about \(P/N=\alpha\). Errors become more likely as \(\alpha\) increases, and retrieval disappears near the classic critical point. The central limit theorem motivates a Gaussian approximation, but the constant 0.138 requires a fuller self-consistent analysis.

diagnostic.prompt: How do asynchronous and synchronous updates differ?
diagnostic.answer: An asynchronous update changes one neuron at a time and immediately uses the new state; a synchronous update changes all neurons simultaneously.
diagnostic.explanation: The classic proof that energy cannot increase depends on asynchronous single-unit updating.

diagnostic.prompt: With symmetric W and \(W_{ii}=0\), how does energy change when one unit flips to follow the sign of its local field?
diagnostic.answer: \(\Delta E=-\Delta S_{i}\) hi. If the update aligns with hi, then \(\Delta E\le 0\).
diagnostic.explanation: Only pair terms involving that unit change, and symmetry combines their two halves.

diagnostic.prompt: Why is \(-\xi\) also usually an attractor when \(P=1\)?
diagnostic.answer: The weights contain products \(\xi _{i}\xi _{j}\) and are unchanged by a global sign flip; at \(-\xi\), the local field again aligns with the current state.
diagnostic.explanation: The classic unbiased model has global sign symmetry.

diagnostic.answer: \(\alpha =P/N=0.1\), below the classic value near 0.138, although finite N still permits errors.
diagnostic.explanation: The critical value is not a hard guarantee for every instance and applies only under the specified dense random assumptions.

diagnostic.prompt: Why is an odd mixture called a spurious memory?
diagnostic.answer: It is formed by the component-wise majority of several stored patterns and may be stable even though it is not any single training pattern.
diagnostic.explanation: Energy minima include more than the intended memories.

modules.title: Explicit memory, Hebbian assemblies, and pattern completion
modules.guidingQuestion: How can a shared-activity cell assembly yield a testable encoding–cue–retrieval chain?
paragraphs: The Hebbian assembly hypothesis proposes that cells jointly active in an experience develop stronger mutual connections. Encoding changes the connections, a partial cue reactivates some members, and recurrent excitation recruits the missing members to complete the pattern. An engram is a cellular ensemble causally involved in memory storage and expression; activation correlation alone is insufficient for that label.

The Hopfield abstraction represents an assembly by binary pattern \(\xi\) and sets \(W_{ij}=(1/N)\sum \mu \xi _{i}^{\mu }\xi _{j}^{\mu }\), with \(W_{ii}=0\). Same-sign pairs receive positive weights and opposite-sign pairs negative weights. Real synapses obey Dale's law and constraints from sparse connectivity and spiking; the classic dense matrix first illustrates a computational principle.

Retrieval cue \(S(0)\) has overlap \(m=(1/N)\sum i\xi iS_{i}\) with the target pattern. \(m=1\) is an exact match, \(m=0\) is uncorrelated on average, and \(m=-1\) is the global antipattern. If the cue lies in the target basin, asynchronous dynamics correct errors progressively. Basin size measures tolerated corruption, not merely whether the fixed point exists.

A causal engram experiment must test sufficiency and necessity separately: does artificial activation of a tagged ensemble trigger memory-like behavior, and does its suppression selectively impair retrieval? Even if both hold, binary Hopfield units and Hebbian weights remain a model mapping; behavior does not identify the exact W directly.
keyPoints: A cell assembly supplies a hypothesis for pattern completion.
The Hopfield outer-product rule is an abstract encoding rule.
Overlap measures cue similarity, whereas a basin measures retrieval robustness.

derivation.title: How overlap responds to cue corruption
derivation.setup: Suppose a fraction f of the target pattern's bits are flipped.

steps.title: Write the contribution of matching bits
steps.explanation: A fraction 1-f of the bits satisfies \(\xi iS_{i}=+1\).

steps.title: Write the contribution of flipped bits
steps.explanation: A fraction f of the bits satisfies \(\xi iS_{i}=-1\).

steps.title: Take the average
steps.explanation: Add both contributions weighted by their fractions.

symbolNotes: m is dimensionless and lies in \([-1,1]\).
f is the fraction flipped and lies in \([0,1]\).
derivation.unitsCheck: Both terms are dimensionless fractions, so overlap is dimensionless.

workedExample.title: Compute overlap for a noisy cue
workedExample.problem: A 100-bit pattern has 20 flipped bits. Find its overlap with the original pattern.
steps: Each of the 80 matching bits contributes +1, totaling 80.
Each of the 20 flipped bits contributes -1, totaling -20.

selfCheck.prompt: Why does \(m>0\) not guarantee successful retrieval?
selfCheck.answer: It measures only similarity at the start. The basin also depends on memory load, the particular crosstalk, update order, and network parameters.

pitfalls: Automatically calling activation-tagged cells a causal engram.
Treating positive overlap as a sufficient condition for success.

modules.title: Binary asynchronous dynamics and stored random patterns
modules.guidingQuestion: When one unit is updated at a time, how is the algorithm executed precisely and convergence determined?
paragraphs: At each step choose i, compute local field \(h_{i}=\sum _j W_{ij} S_{j}\), and set \(S_{i}\leftarrow \operatorname{sgn}(h_{i})\). \(W_{ii}=0\) prevents the unit's own state from voting directly. A tie rule for \(h_{i}=0\) must be specified in advance, such as retaining the old value or choosing a fixed sign. Update order may be random or sequential; different orders can reach different basins, but every step uses the latest state.

One sweep commonly means an average of N updates and does not imply convergence. Stop only after a full check finds no unit that would change or when both state and energy reach a fixed point. A finite deterministic asynchronous system under strict energy descent cannot visit new states forever, although arbitrary flipping on zero-field ties can create degeneracy.

Stored patterns are often independent, unbiased random ±1 vectors for tractable capacity analysis. This is not a statistical model of natural memory: real patterns are correlated and sparse. Correlation increases structured crosstalk but may also support category structure, so randomness is a baseline assumption rather than a fact.

A synchronous update computes every new state from the old state at once and may produce a two-cycle; the classic single-flip energy proof does not apply directly. Code and hand calculations must say whether updates occur in place. Disguising a synchronous vectorized multiplication as asynchronous changes the dynamical conclusion.
keyPoints: An asynchronous update immediately writes back one unit.
Convergence requires a fixed-state check, not a preset number of sweeps.
Unbiased random patterns are an analytical assumption.

derivation.setup: Use an explicit matrix and state to show the local field and in-place writeback.

steps.title: Define the weights and state
steps.explanation: Let \(W_{12}=W_{21}=1\), \(W_{23}=W_{32}=1\), and every other entry equal 0, with initial state \(S=(1,-1,1)\).

steps.title: Update unit 2
steps.explanation: \(h_{2}=S_{1}+S_{3}=2\), so S2 changes from -1 to +1.

steps.title: Update unit 1
steps.explanation: Using the already changed S2, \(h_{1}=S_{2}=1\) and S1 remains +1.

steps.title: Update unit 3

The local field has units weight×state.

derivation.limitCheck: If S2 were not written back immediately on the first step, subsequent fields would differ, demonstrating the importance of the update convention.

workedExample.title: Compute one update by hand

workedExample.sanityCheck: The new state has the same sign as the negative local field.

selfCheck.prompt: Why does updating every neuron once not guarantee a fixed point?
selfCheck.answer: After an early unit is updated, later unit changes can alter its local field, so another complete sweep without changes is required.

pitfalls: Updating all units at once from the old state and calling it asynchronous.

modules.title: Energy descent and the \(P=1\) stored attractor
modules.guidingQuestion: Why do symmetric weights make a single-unit update lower energy, and why are both a stored pattern and its antipattern stable?
paragraphs: Define energy \(E=-(1/2)\sum _i\sum _{j\ne i}W_{ij}S_{i}S_{j}\). The factor 1/2 prevents double-counting a symmetric pair. When only unit i flips, all other pairs are unchanged. Using \(W_{ij}=W_{ji}\) reduces the energy change to \(\Delta E=-\Delta S_{i} h_{i}\). If new \(S_{i}\) aligns with \(h_{i}\), then a flip gives \(\Delta E<0\) and no flip gives 0.

For \(P=1\), let \(W_{ij}=\xi _{i}\xi _{j}/N\). Substituting \(S=\xi\) gives \(h_{i}=(\xi _{i}/N)\sum _{j\ne i}\xi _{j}^{2}=((N-1)/N)\xi _{i}\), so \(\operatorname{sign}(h_{i})=\xi _{i}\) and the pattern is a fixed point. Substituting \(S=-\xi\) gives \(h_{i}=-((N-1)/N)\xi _{i}\), aligned with \(S_{i}=-\xi _{i}\), so the antipattern is stable too.

Nonincreasing energy guarantees arrival at some local minimum, not the global minimum or target memory. A noisy cue may cross a basin boundary and reach a spurious state. Symmetric W is central to the proof. Asymmetric plasticity or delays can generate cycles, chaos, or sequential dynamics, so the same Lyapunov function cannot still be used to claim convergence.

\(W_{ii}=0\) removes self-coupling and subtracts one term from the \(P=1\) field. For large N, (N-1)/N approaches 1, but a small-N example cannot replace it directly by 1. Keeping the finite term teaches the distinction between a finite-size calculation and a large-N approximation.
keyPoints: Symmetric asynchronous dynamics makes energy nonincreasing.
For \(P=1\), \(\xi\) and \(-\xi\) are both stable because of global sign symmetry.
Energy descent does not guarantee retrieval of the desired memory.

steps.explanation: After combining the symmetric pair, the energy involving i is \(-S_{i}\sum _{j\ne i}W_{ij}S_{j}\).

steps.title: Compute the difference
steps.explanation: Subtract old energy from new energy.

steps.title: Update by sign
steps.explanation: If a flip occurs, the new state aligns with \(h_{i}\) and \(\Delta S_{i}\) \(h_{i}>0\).

steps.title: Handle no flip
steps.explanation: If the old state already aligns with the field, \(\Delta S_{i}=0\).

The derivation assumes symmetry and fixed values of all other states during the update.
derivation.unitsCheck: \(\Delta S\) is dimensionless, so multiplying it by h gives energy units.
derivation.limitCheck: When \(h_{i}=0\), \(\Delta E=0\); flipping a tie can move among equal-energy states.

workedExample.title: A finite-N field for \(P=1\)
workedExample.problem: Let \(N=5\) and pattern \(\xi =(1,-1,1,-1,1)\), with the network in \(\xi\). Find the local field of unit1.
steps: The four terms \(\xi _{j}^{2}=1\), so \(h_{1}=4/5=0.8\), aligned with \(\xi _{1}\).
workedExample.sanityCheck: This agrees with the general expression \((N-1)\xi _{1}/N=4/5\).

selfCheck.prompt: Why does the derivation of \(\Delta E\) fail when W is asymmetric?
selfCheck.answer: Pair terms with i as the first and second index cannot be combined into the same local field, so one scalar energy need not decline under updating.

pitfalls: Omitting the energy factor 1/2 and then double-counting pairs.
Automatically calling every local minimum a stored pattern.

modules.title: Spurious mixtures and the signal-plus-crosstalk decomposition
modules.guidingQuestion: When several patterns are stored, how does the local field contain both target signal and interference from other memories?
paragraphs: While retrieving pattern1, set \(S\approx \xi ^{1}\). After substituting Hebbian W, the \(\mu =1\) term of \(h_{i}\) aligns with \(\xi _{i}^{1}\) and is the signal; terms with \(\mu >1\) contain random overlaps and form crosstalk. Even when every interference pattern is orthogonal to the target on average, finite-N overlap is nonzero, and many small terms can flip individual bits.

An odd mixture can be written \(S_{i}=\operatorname{sgn}(\xi _{i}^{1}+\xi _{i}^{2}+\xi _{i}^{3})\). A component-wise vote among three patterns has no tie and can be self-consistent under the Hebbian field. The mixture is not any one input training pattern but can be a fixed point, shrinking usable basins and causing erroneous combinatorial recall.

A two-pattern mixture has component ties, so stability depends more strongly on the tie rule and bias; odd mixtures are more typical in the dense unbiased model. Pattern correlations produce structured mixtures, so not every false memory should be attributed to independent Gaussian noise. Identify a spurious state by comparing its overlap with every stored pattern, not by low energy alone.

Basin boundaries shrink as P increases. A cue can have its highest overlap with the target and still flow to a mixture because all stored patterns jointly shape the energy landscape. Any analogy to experimental 'memory blending' is only a hypothesis; real memory distortion also depends on semantic inference, overlap during encoding, and systems consolidation.
keyPoints: A local field separates into target-aligned signal and crosstalk from multiple memories.
An odd component-wise majority can form a spurious attractor.
Neither the lowest energy nor the highest initial overlap guarantees target retrieval.

steps.explanation: Insert the P outer products into the local field.

steps.explanation: The target term is approximately \(\xi _{i}^{1}\).

steps.title: Name the remaining term

workedExample.problem: At one unit, three patterns have bits (+1,+1,-1). Find the odd-mixture bit. What if they are (+1,-1,-1)?

selfCheck.answer: Correctness is defined by the training target and behavioral identity; energy determines dynamical stability and does not know which patterns were designated as memories.

modules.title: Gaussian crosstalk, loading, and classic capacity
modules.guidingQuestion: Why does \(\alpha =P/N\) control the scale of random interference, and why is 0.138 not a universal constant for every associative memory?
paragraphs: For independent unbiased patterns, one nontarget overlap \(\sum _j\xi _{j}^{\mu }\xi _{j}^{1}\) has \(\operatorname{mean} 0\) and variance approximately N. After multiplication by 1/N, one pattern contributes field variance of about 1/N. Summing P-1 nearly independent terms gives crosstalk variance \((P-1)/N\approx \alpha\). This motivates a Gaussian-noise approximation through the central limit theorem.

A target bit is stable when \(\xi _{i}^{1}h_{i}>0\): unit-aligned signal 1 plus noise remains positive. If \(\mathrm{noise}\approx N(0,\alpha )\), the single-step error is approximately \(\Phi (-1/\sqrt \alpha )\) and rises with \(\alpha\). Unit errors feed back into the fields, so full self-consistency gives the classic dense-model retrieval threshold \(\alpha c\) of about 0.138 rather than the simple single-step tail alone.

P can grow linearly with N, but 'capacity=Pmax' depends on the retrieval criterion, acceptable error, and basin size. The value 0.138 assumes symmetric dense connectivity, unbiased independent random ±1 patterns, Hebbian weights, and classic dynamics. Sparse codes, correlated patterns, alternative rules, or finite N change the number.

A spin-glass regime still has many stable states but little overlap with any stored pattern; the network converges without retrieving. Checking energy convergence alone misclassifies success. Also measure target overlap, bit error, basin volume, and trial-to-trial outcomes.
keyPoints: Crosstalk variance is approximately the loading \(\alpha\).
The Gaussian tail gives an error tendency; the complete critical value requires self-consistency.
Convergence and retrieval are distinct evaluation criteria.

derivation.setup: Assume independent, unbiased patterns and neglect finite-index correlations.

steps.explanation: A sum of N independent ±1 products has \(\operatorname{mean} 0\) and variance N.

steps.title: Include 1/N
steps.explanation: Divide the variance of one pattern's field contribution by \(N^{2}\).

steps.title: \(\operatorname{Sum} P-1\) terms
steps.explanation: Independent variances add.

steps.explanation: For large N, use \(\alpha =P/N\).

\(z\mu\) is the contribution of one nontarget pattern to the aligned field.

workedExample.problem: Let \(\alpha =0.25\), \(\mathrm{signal}=1\), and noise standard deviation \(\sqrt \alpha =0.5\). An error requires \(\mathrm{noise}<-1\), equivalent to standard \(\operatorname{normal} Z<-2\).

selfCheck.prompt: Why does \(\alpha =0.1\) below 0.138 still not guarantee success for every cue?
selfCheck.answer: The threshold is a large-N typical statistic under a particular retrieval criterion. Finite patterns, poor cues, basin differences, and random instances can still fail.

pitfalls: Treating 0.138 as the capacity ratio of every biological memory.
Passing off a one-step Gaussian tail calculation as the full critical derivation.

modules.title: Sparse stochastic associative memory and global inhibition
modules.guidingQuestion: When a dense ±1 code becomes sparse \({0,1}\) activity, why must threshold, inhibition, and capacity analyses be rewritten?
paragraphs: Real ensembles often activate only a fraction a of their units. With \(\xi _{i}\in {0,1}\) and \(P(active)=a\), pattern mean is nonzero. The Hebbian rule should center \(\xi _{i}-a\) to prevent a large positive bias shared by all units. Retrieval can use a probabilistic logistic output rather than a hard sign, with temperature controlling stochasticity.

Original Page 6 places global inhibition directly in every weight by subtracting \(\gamma /(aN)\) after the centered Hebbian term. In the local field, this uniform negative term becomes \(-(\gamma /(aN))\sum _jS_{j}\), so a larger active population imposes stronger inhibition on every unit. Together with stochastic threshold u, it constrains total activity near aN. It is not one particular inhibitory neuron; rewriting it as an adaptive threshold requires an explicit mapping to population activity.

Sparse codes reduce active overlap between patterns and can improve information per synapse or some capacity measures. Any claim of 'near-optimality' must say whether it measures patterns/neuron, bits/synapse, or retrieval error. A dense-model \(\alpha c=0.138\) cannot be compared directly with one sparse-model number without matching activity and metrics.

As temperature \(T\to 0\), a probabilistic update approaches a deterministic threshold. With large T, states become more random and may escape shallow minima. Stochasticity can aid sampling but also impairs stable recall. Evaluate an alternative model with false-positive and false-negative rates, overlap distributions, and capacity as a function of a, T, and inhibition, not only maximum P.
keyPoints: Sparse patterns require mean subtraction or threshold control.
Capacity comparisons must use the same information and error metrics.

workedExample.problem: Let sparsity \(a=0.1\). What are the centered values of an active bit and an inactive bit, and what is their product?

selfCheck.prompt: Why does an uncentered 0/1 Hebbian rule produce a global positive bias?

Claiming higher sparse capacity without stating the units of comparison.

synthesis: The Hopfield model abstracts explicit memory as attractor dynamics: recurrent updates drive a partial cue toward a stored pattern. Symmetric weights and asynchronous single-neuron updates ensure that Ising energy cannot increase. For \(P=1\), Hebbian weights make both the target and its sign-reversed pattern fixed points. questions.explanation: The Hebbian assembly hypothesis proposes that cells jointly active in an experience develop stronger mutual connections. Encoding changes the connections, a partial cue reactivates some members, and recurrent excitation recruits the missing members to complete the pattern. An engram is a cellular ensemble causally involved in memory storage and expression; activation correlation alone is insufficient for that label. Same-sign pairs receive positive weights and opposite-sign pairs negative weights. Real synapses obey Dale's law and constraints from sparse connectivity and spiking; the classic dense matrix first illustrates a computational principle.
